item.stem:
Which model describes the therapist's role this way?

“non acceptance”

options.sourceLine: Change happens through the existential encounter – the authentic meeting of the therapist and the client in the present moment and by expanding the client’s range of experience. Very influenced by Gestalt therapy. Generally used with families, started by Carl Whittaker.

Change occurs through finding meaning, living authentically and responsibly. The idea that the person can respond, make choices, emphasizes personal choice about how clients want to live their lives. Core question: how do I exist? Inherent meaninglessness to life and existence.

The idea is that change occurs through increased awareness of here and now experience and dialogic relationship between T and client. Dialogic refers to a therapeutic stance where the therapist and client engage as two authentic human beings — fully present with each other, co-creating the therapeutic process. Heavily influenced by Martin Buber’s “I-Thou” philosophy, where the therapist meets the client as a fellow human, not an object to be treated.
non acceptance

options.sourceLine: Scaling Questions: The therapist asks the client to think of a scale ranging from the worst things could be to the best. The client then rates their current position on the scale and is asked to identify how they could move up or down the scale. The client is also encouraged to identify what point on the scale would be good enough or where their “perfect future” is. Example: “You said that things are between a 4 and a 5. What would need to happen so that things were between a 5 and 6?”

Coping Questions: If a client has trouble identifying positive change, coping questions are asked by the therapist in order to illustrate resources that the client already has. This can include validating the client’s difficulties while also showing that they are still able to get up in the morning, go to school, etc. This highlights the client’s strengths without undermining their view of reality. These questions are supportive while also challenging the client and shifting the focus away from problem-focused narratives. Example: “How do you keep going each day even when it feels like there is no hope?”

item.stem: “Repair stage” is a signature term of which model?

options.sourceLine: Change occurs through both reparative experiences within the treatment relationship (relationship with therapist) insight into and modification of entrenched object relations pathology.
Change occurs through empathetic attunement and strengthening the self-structures through optimal responsiveness. Shift away from interpretation.

Repair stage of the therapy aims to alter the patient’s current reactions to the events that cause them emotional distress by sharing their own interpretations of the event. By sharing their own subjective interpretation, the therapist helps create a new reality of the painful events for the patient in order to get rid of unwanted emotions and reactions.

Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.

item.rationale: Repair stage belongs to Attachment-Based Therapy (Bowlby) and is not claimed by any other model in the packet.

item.stem: “Focus on moment to moment” is a signature term of which model?

options.sourceLine: Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.
Focus on moment to moment during therapy, process not content.

The idea is that change occurs through increased awareness of here and now experience and dialogic relationship between T and client. Dialogic refers to a therapeutic stance where the therapist and client engage as two authentic human beings — fully present with each other, co-creating the therapeutic process. Heavily influenced by Martin Buber’s “I-Thou” philosophy, where the therapist meets the client as a fellow human, not an object to be treated.

Change happens through the existential encounter – the authentic meeting of the therapist and the client in the present moment and by expanding the client’s range of experience. Very influenced by Gestalt therapy. Generally used with families, started by Carl Whittaker.

item.rationale: Focus on moment to moment belongs to Existential Therapy and is not claimed by any other model in the packet.
